_about: Every URL consulted while checking something, with what it settles and what it bears on. Not a reading list — a reading list says what is worth reading, this says what was actually used and for which claim.
_rule: `description` records the question the page answered, not what the page is about. A source with no link into the concept, algorithm, implementation or technology layers has no reason to be here.

_relations.defines: The origin of the idea, or the place it is given its standard form.
_relations.describes: Explains the mechanism without being its origin — a survey, a tutorial, a course text.
_relations.verifies: Was used to check a specific fact: a year, an author, a version, a package's existence.
_relations.corrects: Overturned something this catalogue previously asserted.
_relations.disputes: Contests a claim that other sources make. Recorded rather than resolved.
_relations.implements: Code that is the reference for the method.

sources.title: Fast Hydraulic Erosion Simulation and Visualization on GPU
sources.description: Settled whether erosion is inherently an offline process. It is not: the pipe-model formulation of shallow-water flow, erosion, transport and deposition runs entirely on the GPU at interactive rates, which is why the concept card's "minutes to hours" claim had to be narrowed to CPU implementations.

links.note: Overturned the claim that erosion cannot be iterated interactively.

sources.title: Visual Models of Plants Interacting with Their Environment
sources.description: Establishes that L-systems can be environmentally aware. Open L-systems exchange information bidirectionally with a program modelling the environment, which is how collision between branches, competition for light and pruning are handled — so the blanket claim that L-systems cannot do global awareness only holds for the context-free form.

links.note: Narrowed the "no global awareness" limitation to context-free L-systems.

sources.title: Curl-Noise for Procedural Fluid Flow
sources.description: Shows curl noise is a construction over a noise field, not a noise basis: the velocity field is the curl of a potential built from Perlin noise, which is what makes it exactly divergence-free without solving a linear system. Used to move curl out of the list of noise bases in the concept card.

links.note: Curl noise was listed alongside Perlin and Worley as if it were an alternative to them.

sources.title: A chiral aperiodic monotile
sources.description: The reason the hat and the spectre are not interchangeable. Hat tilings need reflected copies; the spectre family admits only chiral non-periodic tilings, so it tiles without its mirror image. Decides whether a one-sided or physically cut tile set can be built from a single shape.

links.note: The concept card implied the hat alone suffices for aperiodic coverage.

sources.title: WaveFunctionCollapse — reference implementation and README
sources.description: The specification for what people mean by WFC, since there is no paper. Settles three things: adjacency is learned from N×N patterns in one bitmap, propagation is AC-4 with a minimum-entropy choice heuristic, and a contradiction ends the run — there is no backtracking. Also states the generalisation of Merrell's model synthesis from tiles to overlapping patterns.

links.note: Named AC-4 and minimum entropy; removed the implication that the canonical implementation backtracks.
States what WFC changed relative to Merrell.

sources.title: A particle method for history-dependent materials
sources.publisher: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering 118, 179–196
sources.description: Settles the origin of the material point method, which this catalogue had dated to the 2013 graphics paper. It also names the lineage: MPM is an extension of the particle-in-cell code FLIP from fluids to solid mechanics, the addition being that each material point carries the full stress tensor. FLIP is separately an entry here, so the mis-dating had hidden a link inside the catalogue's own table.

links.note: Nineteen years earlier than the date recorded, and the parent method was already in the table.
Named as the method MPM extends.

sources.title: Quadtree — region, point and point-region variants
sources.description: Used to separate two structures that share one name. Region quadtrees are Klinger 1971, the term in this sense is from Hunter's 1978 Princeton thesis, and octree encoding is Meagher 1980; Finkel & Bentley 1974 — which this catalogue was citing — is the point quadtree, which splits at data points rather than at midpoints. Graphics uses the region variety.

links.note: The entry described a region quadtree while citing the point quadtree paper.

sources.title: Eller's Algorithm — Mazes for Programmers
sources.description: The source the catalogue already cited for Eller's algorithm, read properly: it dates the algorithm to 1982, not 1980, and describes it as combining Sidewinder's row-at-a-time structure with Kruskal's set-merging to avoid Sidewinder's bias.

sources.title: Texturing & Modeling: A Procedural Approach — contents
sources.publisher: Ebert, Musgrave, Peachey, Perlin & Worley; Academic Press
sources.description: Fixes the date on ridged multifractal, and is the right link for a citation whose point is that it is a book chapter rather than a paper. The first edition is 1994; the catalogue said 1993 and linked to Wikipedia's article on fractional Brownian motion, which is the thing ridged multifractal modifies and says nothing about the modification.

links.note: Also the documented source for value noise, which has no origin paper.

sources.title: Priority-Flood: An Optimal Depression-Filling and Watershed-Labeling Algorithm for Digital Elevation Models
sources.description: Justifies flow routing as a concept in its own right rather than a step inside erosion. Depression filling has an optimal algorithm — O(n) for integer elevations — that is separate from any transport model, and the authors note the whole thing is under 100 lines of C++. That combination of importable, standard and short is what the concept vocabulary was missing.

links.note: The precondition step: without it, routing on real noisy data terminates in local pits.

sources.title: RichDEM — high-performance terrain analysis
sources.description: The named importable that lets flow routing pass the concept test: depression filling, D8 and multiple-flow-direction routing, flow accumulation and watershed labelling, in one installable package rather than as a paper to reimplement.

sources.title: A perceptual color space for image processing (Oklab)
sources.description: Why colour needed a concept of its own: the choice of space decides whether a generated gradient has a grey dead zone in the middle, and Ottosson shows the failure side by side. Also the origin of the space that CSS and every design-token generator now use for interpolation.

sources.title: CSS Color Module Level 4
sources.description: Makes the colour concept importable in the strongest possible sense — the perceptual spaces, difference metrics and interpolation rules are shipped in every browser, so a palette generator does not need a library at all. Used to check that Oklab, Lab, LCH and the interpolation behaviour are specified rather than conventions.

sources.title: Texture Synthesis by Non-parametric Sampling
sources.description: The origin of growing a texture pixel by pixel by matching neighbourhoods against a single example, and the reason example-based synthesis is a concept rather than a trick: no model is fitted at all, the sample *is* the model. Establishes the family that WFC later generalises.

sources.title: OpenSubdiv — introduction and documentation
sources.description: The importable that makes subdivision a block: Catmull–Clark and Loop with semi-sharp creases, hierarchical edits and GPU evaluation, in the library that Maya, Blender and RenderMan all use — so it is the de facto specification of what subdivision means in practice, not just one implementation of it.

sources.title: A 99 line topology optimization code written in Matlab
sources.description: The reason topology optimisation is defensible as a block despite having no mature library: the specification is 99 lines, split 36 main / 12 optimality-criteria optimiser / 16 mesh-independency filter / 35 finite elements. Andreassen et al. later cut it to 88 by vectorising. A method whose complete reference implementation fits on two pages does not need a package to be pinned down.

sources.title: Efficient topology optimization in MATLAB using 88 lines of code
sources.description: Checked to confirm the shorter figure quoted for SIMP: 88 lines, reached from Sigmund's 99 by preallocating arrays and vectorising loops rather than by cutting functionality. Fixes the line count this catalogue quotes.

sources.title: PyPI metadata for `pymo` — a name collision, not a motion library
sources.description: Checked while testing whether data-driven motion synthesis could pass the importable test. PyPI `pymo` is "MongoClient instrumentation and factory", not the motion-capture package the name suggests — the same failure mode that put `sdf` (Scientific Data Format) and `wfc` (WebForms Core) in this catalogue's caveat list. PyPI `meep` is likewise a task runner, not the MIT photonics solver. Both are why the motion concept was rejected rather than asserted.

links.note: The nearest existing concept to the rejected `motion` addition.

sources.title: Unity — AsyncGPUReadback
sources.description: Documents the actual cost of getting shader-generated data back to the CPU: the asynchronous path copies without stalling either processor but adds a few frames of latency. Used to replace "the CPU never sees it" with the real trade-off.

links.note: Readback exists; what is true is that it costs a stall or a few frames.

sources.title: GitHub API metadata for FastNoiseLite
sources.description: The check that closed this catalogue's stated method gap. The README said registry verification could not reach GitHub-hosted C++ and named FastNoiseLite, Recast, mxgmn's WFC and CGAL as examples; api.github.com/repos returns licence, last push and archive status, which is enough to verify a row to the same standard as npm or PyPI. All four are now recorded.

links.note: The technology that had nothing attached to it before this check existed.

sources.title: crates.io API metadata for the `noise` crate
sources.description: How the Rust rows were resolved. crates.io reports max_stable_version separately from max_version, which matters: taking the latest version alone would record a pre-release as the current one.

sources.title: NuGet flat container index for QuikGraph
sources.description: How the C# rows were resolved. The flat container lists every published version but does not mark which are pre-releases, so they have to be filtered by the hyphen in the semantic version — otherwise a release candidate is recorded as current.

sources.title: npm registry metadata for noisejs
sources.description: The row that disproved this catalogue's own explanation of its release dates. The file guessed the clustered 2022 dates were a bulk registry operation and advised against reading them as abandonment; the registry says noisejs 2.1.0 was published in 2013 and nothing has shipped since. The dates had been filled with the lookup date, and the wrong dates were hiding real abandonment.

sources.title: Image Quilting for Texture Synthesis and Transfer
sources.description: Separates the two ideas usually conflated when people say "quilting": copying patches instead of pixels, which bought two orders of magnitude of speed, and cutting each seam along a minimum-cost path instead of blending it, which bought quality blending cannot. Used to put the texsyn progression in the right order.

sources.title: PatchMatch: A Randomized Correspondence Algorithm for Structural Image Editing
sources.description: Settles why every earlier texture-synthesis method suddenly became interactive around 2009: not a better synthesiser, but a cheap approximate nearest-neighbour field. Random initialisation, propagation from already-scanned neighbours, and random search at decreasing radii.

sources.title: Surface Simplification Using Quadric Error Metrics
sources.description: The algorithm that decides what all generated geometry looks like at a distance, since it is what every automatic LOD chain runs. Establishes that the error can be accumulated per vertex as a 4x4 quadratic form rather than recomputed against the original mesh, which is what keeps it cheap.

sources.title: Instant Field-Aligned Meshes
sources.description: Answers the catalogue entry "Remeshing & retopology", which had no method attached. Two local smoothing problems — an orientation field, then a position field — replace a global parameterisation, which is why it runs interactively on million-triangle meshes where earlier methods did not.

sources.title: Poisson Surface Reconstruction
sources.description: Why photogrammetry and LiDAR pipelines all produce watertight, slightly soft meshes: the reconstruction is a global least-squares fit of a gradient field, so noise averages out and holes get filled by the smoothest continuation — including holes that should have stayed open.

sources.title: Poisson Image Editing
sources.description: Establishes the gradient-domain half of seam removal, complementary to the pixel-selection half that graph-cut textures solve. Transferring gradients rather than values lets an inserted region relight itself to its surroundings, which is why the seam vanishes without feathering.

sources.title: Bilateral Filtering for Gray and Color Images
sources.description: The one extra term that turns a blur into an edge-preserving operator, and therefore the basis of the detail-layer split used throughout texture authoring: filter a heightfield, subtract, and the large forms separate from the fine grain without the halos a Gaussian split produces.

sources.title: Sphere Tracing: A Geometric Method for the Antialiased Ray Tracing of Implicit Surfaces
sources.description: The step the sdf concept was missing: five polygonisers were recorded and nothing about rendering a distance field directly. Sphere tracing is what makes an SDF interesting — no tessellation, no acceleration structure, and booleans and infinite repetition become one-line changes.

sources.title: Breaking Paragraphs into Lines
sources.description: The entry this catalogue’s README claimed was in the algorithm layer while it was not. Also settles where it belongs: the mechanism is a shortest path through a directed acyclic graph of feasible breakpoints, which puts it under graph algorithms rather than typesetting.

sources.title: Arc and Path Consistency Revisited
sources.description: The propagation algorithm WFC actually uses. Per-value support counters instead of re-examining whole arcs, which reaches the optimal worst case and is exactly the "compatible neighbour count" bookkeeping WFC implementations are full of. Without this row the catalogue named AC-3, which WFC does not use.

sources.title: Improving Noise
sources.description: Establishes that "Perlin noise" names two different algorithms. The 1985 cubic fade has a non-zero second derivative at the ends, so derived normal maps show discontinuities on lattice planes; the 2002 quintic fixes that, and the 12 fixed edge-midpoint gradients fix the directional bias. Almost every library implements the 2002 version while citing the 1985 paper.

sources.title: Wavelet Turbulence for Fluid Simulation
sources.description: Why film smoke pipelines are "simulate low, upres high". The energy at unresolved scales can be extrapolated from Kolmogorov’s k^-5/3 law rather than computed, and synthesised as divergence-free curl noise — which makes this entry depend directly on another already in the table.

sources.title: Growing Neural Cellular Automata
sources.description: The bridge between the ca and ml concepts, and a genuinely different point on the trade-off: a few thousand parameters rather than a few hundred million, and self-repair after damage learned rather than designed. Also the clearest demonstration that a CA rule can be fitted instead of invented.

sources.title: PCGRL: Procedural Content Generation via Reinforcement Learning
sources.description: Answers the ml concept card’s own complaint that PCGML fails where you have forty training examples: this needs none, because the reward function supplies the signal. It also moves the expensive part to training time, so generation afterwards is a forward pass rather than a search.
